acceptance_checks.description: files holds exactly 10000 documents for ns=demo, item-per-document 1:1 with the ns-filtered DynamoDB scan, with deterministic _id (uuid5 of the source key).
The DynamoDB ns attribute becomes an indexed tenant field on every document; no document is written without it.
DynamoDB attribute types map without loss: N to a numeric BSON type (no float drift on sizes), BOOL to boolean, B to BSON binary, and absent attributes are omitted rather than written as null.
The source scan is fully paginated: recon proves the migrated count equals the summed page counts, so a truncated scan cannot pass as green.
The 40 orphaned metadata items (no owning document) are migrated but flagged and enumerated as orphaned_metadata; they are never deleted or re-parented.
files carries a $jsonSchema validator requiring the tenant field, a string storage key, and a date-typed modified timestamp; a legacy string date is rejected with server error 121.
Recon recomputes the manifest checksum db614663b2c6d41141cae82261b416d5 from the Atlas collection and matches it exactly.
Re-running the migration for ns=demo reproduces identical counts, checksum, and orphan set with no duplicates.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Storage keys and filenames are carried through byte-for-byte, including spaces and non-ASCII characters; no URL-encoding, lowercasing, or path normalization.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: An S attribute that cannot be decoded as UTF-8 is quarantined with reason invalid_encoding and its raw bytes recorded as hex; B attributes are stored as BSON binary.

malformed_record_policy.details: Unknown extra DynamoDB attributes are preserved in a named extras subdocument and attributed in the recon report. A missing ns, storage key, or timestamp is never defaulted: the item is quarantined with a reason code.

empty_input_semantics.details: An empty ns-filtered scan leaves prior files untouched and exits zero; it never clears the collection.

planted_anomalies.description: 40 orphaned dynamodb.file-metadata items must be surfaced as an exact set of 40 flagged documents.
1 missing S3 event hour under s3.data-lake/events/demo/ is planted in the legacy estate but no MongoDB workload ingests the S3 event lake this run.
planted_anomalies.reason: The S3 event lake is not part of the document model being migrated to Atlas (customers, invoices, documents, files); it is claimed by the Databricks track, so no unit reads it and the anomaly is intentionally uncovered here.
